title: Remove Previously Seen Anagrams
statement:
You are given a list of `n` lowercase words. Two words are **anagrams** of each other if one can be rearranged into the other, that is, they contain exactly the same letters with the same counts. A word that is identical to an earlier word is also an anagram of it.

Scan the list from left to right and remove every word that is an anagram of a word that appears **earlier** in the list. The first word of each anagram group is kept. Return the words that remain, sorted in ascending lexicographic (dictionary) order.

At least one word always remains, because the first word is never removed.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The next `n` tokens are the words, separated by whitespace (one per line).
outputFormat: Print the remaining words in sorted order, separated by single spaces, on one line.
constraints: Words consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: `doce` and `ecod` are rearrangements of the earlier word `code`, so both are removed. `framer` is kept first, and `frame` has different letters (it lacks the extra `r`), so it is kept too. The survivors `code`, `framer`, `frame` sorted give `code frame framer`.

examples.input:
6
listen
silent
banana
abnnaa
enlist
cab
examples.explanation: `silent` and `enlist` are anagrams of `listen`; `abnnaa` is an anagram of `banana`. What remains is `listen`, `banana`, `cab`, which sorted is `banana cab listen`.
The second `ab` is identical to an earlier word and `ba` is a rearrangement of it, so both are removed. `b` is a different group and stays.

complexity.time: O(n · L log L), L = max word length

hints: Two words are anagrams exactly when they have the same canonical form. What simple transformation of a word gives the same result for every rearrangement?
Keep a hash set of canonical forms already seen while scanning left to right; only keep a word whose form is new.
Sort the kept words at the end, not while scanning: the removal rule depends on the original order.
